bib.title: Chapter 7: High-Fidelity RAG and Defense: The NASA-Inspired Research Assistant (Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Systems)
bib.venue: Packt book chapter (read via O'Reilly, printed 12/26/25)

question: How can a plan-and-execute multi-agent context engine give cited, verifiable RAG answers and be protected against data poisoning and prompt injection from its knowledge base?
contributions: Ingestion pipeline separated from the engine, storing source filename as metadata on every chunk
helper_sanitize_input regex gateway between retrieval and synthesis
Citation-aware Researcher agent that appends sources programmatically
Backward-compatibility validation of the engine on the Chapter 5 and 6 examples, with a function inventory and mind maps

results.claim: Retrieval returns the top 3 chunks per researcher query.
results.setup: agent_researcher calls query_pinecone with top_k=3 on namespace KnowledgeStore; embedding model text-embedding-3-small, generation model gpt-5

results.claim: The Planner produced a six-step plan (Librarian, Researcher x2, Librarian, Writer x2) for the Juno query; one run, no metrics.

results.claim: The sanitizer is a basic static pattern list that the author says must be extended extensively; model-based safety systems are recommended in production.

results.claim: On an Apollo 11 query against a knowledge base holding only Juno and Perseverance documents, the Researcher reported absence of information instead of fabricating.
results.setup: Chapter 5 backward-compatibility test, single run, gpt-5; qualitative
results.quote:
Instead of fabricating data, the Researcher agent truthfully reports the

results.claim: The researcher output lists both juno_mission_overview.txt and perseverance_rover_tools.txt as sources although it cites only [1], because all unique retrieved sources are appended.
results.setup: Trace output of the Juno query; sources taken from retrieved chunk metadata, not from the LLM
results.note: The chapter calls this proof that high-fidelity RAG works; it does not remark that the second source is unused.

limits: No quantitative evaluation: two toy documents, single runs, no retrieval or citation accuracy metrics
Sanitizer is regex only; author concedes it is basic and must be extended
Appending all retrieved sources records what was retrieved, not what was used
LLM output is stochastic and may vary between runs (author note)
Chapter says a production system should add moderation APIs, guardrails or prompt shielding
practices: Separate the data ingestion pipeline from the context engine, as a data management department would (Architecting section).
Store the source document name in each chunk's metadata at ingestion so every claim can be traced (Part 1).
Verify after ingestion that the metadata is stored and retrieved, with a probe query (Verification).
Sanitize retrieved text before it reaches the synthesis LLM and drop failing chunks (Part 2).
Use a citation-aware prompt and append the unique sources programmatically so the list stays complete if the LLM omits one (Part 2).
Instruct the agent to answer only from the provided sources so that it reports missing information (Chapter 5 test case).
Run backward-compatibility tests of earlier chapters' workflows after each upgrade; keep agent output contracts readable by the consumer (trilingual Writer).
Keep a complete function inventory and mind map of the engine (Validation section).
Offer the user a choice between strict context adherence and general model help on a negative result (Chapter 5 test case).

terms.definition: an attack where malicious instructions, hidden within the data retrieved by the RAG system, are used to trick or hijack the final language model into performing an unintended action.
an attacker first manages to get malicious text into the vector database (stage 1 of a two-stage attack, followed by prompt injection via RAG)
a technique that goes beyond simple retrieval to provide verifiable citations for its synthesized answers
a Writer able to process three data contracts: 'facts', 'summary' and 'answer_with_sources'
